requirements.requirement: Join node2's and node3's segments (seg-a via eth1, seg-b via eth2 on node1) into a single L2 broadcast domain, with node1 forwarding frames as a bridge rather than routing between them
requirements.summary: node1 created br0 with eth1 and eth2 as bridge members in 'forwarding' state (cmd-0b1b535e92724f81). br0 itself has no IPv4 address, and node1's bridge fdb table shows both node2's and node3's real host MAC addresses learned dynamically on the correct bridge ports (cmd-0c3be32e35da46c2), which is direct evidence of pure L2 switching rather than L3 routing.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 share one subnet
requirements.summary: node2's enp8s0 was configured with 192.168.50.11/24 and node3's enp8s0 with 192.168.50.12/24, both on the same /24 (cmd-81c0c6fe4ed7409a, cmd-776b3d492b27465e).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 reach each other directly (on-link, no gateway hop through node1's IP stack)
requirements.summary: Ping from node2 to node3 succeeded with 0% loss, and 'ip route get' showed the destination resolved via the directly connected interface with no gateway, confirming an on-link L2 path rather than a routed hop (cmd-ddc4a2a9ae14403c).

requirements.requirement: Bridge and IP configuration persists (survives reboot)
requirements.summary: node1's bridge config was written to /etc/network/interfaces.d/br0 and validated with ifquery (cmd-16541490478344aa, cmd-cd71d2296ad7493c), with bridge-utils/ifupdown hooks confirmed present (cmd-79220080499448f3). node2/node3 static IPs were applied via nmcli with autoconnect=yes. This was subsequently proven durable by the actual reboot of all three nodes, after which the bridge, IPs, and connectivity were all observed intact (cmd-7770ad3d01d846a2, cmd-5dc11114c6c34438, cmd-402ff8cd87784450).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node1 baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered bridging/connectivity
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id e5168e03 with healthy bridge captured (cmd-c9ff58a6ef45433d), reboot issued (cmd-eacd0f79a6274520), post-restart boot_id dd8f941e confirmed changed (cmd-60dd81b8a5fe47f7) matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, bridge/eth1/eth2 auto-reformed (cmd-7770ad3d01d846a2), and node2->node3 ping plus fdb MAC relearning confirmed recovery (cmd-24f34503d5d74071, cmd-e98a33dcdac34ce0).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node2 baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 739c9792 with IP/connectivity captured (cmd-40d39fcd75d34f47), reboot issued (cmd-c6e523235b8d4518), post-restart boot_id 34db947a confirmed changed (cmd-7e2210b172234643) matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, and static IP plus ping to node3 confirmed recovered (cmd-5dc11114c6c34438).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart protocol: node3 baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id aad96cc9 with IP/connectivity captured (cmd-074606e2c71040bd), reboot issued (cmd-bb3064c371e44681), post-restart boot_id 788626cc confirmed changed (cmd-d10bc2fc179441ab) matching the fixed after_executor snapshot, static IP plus ping to node2 confirmed recovered, and node1's fdb/link state reconfirmed both peers relearned after all three restarts (cmd-402ff8cd87784450, cmd-29affdfdf6d04648).

overall_summary: The executor built a Linux bridge (br0) on node1 spanning eth1 and eth2, giving node2 and node3 a shared 192.168.50.0/24 subnet with no IP on the bridge itself. Direct evidence (bridge fdb MAC learning, gateway-less on-link routing, and successful pings) confirms node1 is forwarding frames at L2 rather than routing, fully satisfying the task's material outcome. Configuration was persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d and NetworkManager profiles, and this was proven durable through an actual reboot of all three nodes, each showing a changed boot identity (cross-checked against the fixed after-executor snapshots) followed by confirmed recovery of the bridge, IP configuration, and connectivity. One minor, low-risk, unrelated mutation (docker0 interface teardown) was identified as unnecessary hygiene residue but did not affect the outcome.
limitations: The docker0 address/link mutation in cmd-979cfc2d215b4d2d is not directly tied to the seg-a/seg-b bridging task; its purpose is not explained in the trace, so its necessity could not be fully verified beyond inference from context.
MTU is 9122 on eth1/eth2 while enp8s0 on node2/node3 uses default 1500; this does not affect the demonstrated ping/L2-forwarding evidence but was not explicitly reconciled by the executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands were purposeful: bridge creation/cleanup on node1 (cmd-0b1b535e92724f81), IP assignment on node2/node3 (cmd-81c0c6fe4ed7409a, cmd-776b3d492b27465e), config persistence writes (cmd-16541490478344aa, cmd-cd71d2296ad7493c), and the three scheduled reboots (cmd-eacd0f79a6274520, cmd-c6e523235b8d4518, cmd-bb3064c371e44681) all map directly to the task or the restart protocol. One command (cmd-979cfc2d215b4d2d) deleted the IPv4 address from node1's unrelated docker0 interface and set it down, plus flushed any global-scope addresses on eth1/eth2; docker0 was already observed down/unused at baseline and is not part of either segment being bridged, so this mutation has no clear causal link to the task outcome. It was low-risk (docker0 was already down and disconnected) and left no functional residue, so it is treated as a minor, bounded unnecessary mutation rather than a serious hygiene issue.
